lesson: Notice where it begins. Not with mourning already arrived, but with the fog before it, waking is a slow arithmetic. It enters inside the body half asleep, because that's the honest starting point, and it lets you feel the weight before it means anything. Watch how the images hand off. The warm dark under the blanket becomes cold floor, and the floor argues. Then that heaviness in the body quietly turns into a heaviness that wants sorting. A pile you keep circling. That's the sleight of hand, physical weight, becoming the weight of a day's tasks, and you barely feel the seam. The turn comes when light arrives the color of poured tea, asking nothing you can't give. Picture becomes meaning right there. The day is a thing your hands must reach. Here's what to steal. Let one plain object carry the whole feeling. Feed on a cold floor. Do more than any statement could.
